title: Tenant-aware replica routing and cost-shepherding for shadow traffic
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: implement a tenant-aware replica routing pipeline that safely duplicates a configurable fraction of online traffic to candidate model variants while enforcing per-tenant cost budgets, strict isolation, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers design and initial implementation of the routing policy engine, adaptive sampling, tenant budget accounting, and quarantine behavior for misbehaving tenants or models.

Background: previous shadowing efforts showed two recurring problems: (1) uncontrolled cost growth when large tenants were sampled naively, and (2) noisy signals when KV-cache effects made candidate responses non-representative. We need a production-grade primitive that prevents runaway spend, preserves tenant isolation, and produces useful evaluation signals for canary and A/B workflows.

Proposed approach:
- Replica routing layer: add a lightweight routing service that takes existing request metadata (tenant_id, route, priority, sequence_length_hint) and decides whether to replicate the request to N candidate backends. Decisions are policy-driven (fractional sampling, budget tokens, explicit allowlist/denylist).
- Tenant budgets and accounting: maintain a rough online ledger per tenant that decrements budget tokens on replicated requests using an estimated cost-per-token or cost-per-request model. Budgets are configurable per-tenant and per-environment (dev/stage/prod). When budget drained, replication is disabled for that tenant until manual top-up or cycle reset.
- Adaptive sampling: sampling fraction is adaptive based on three signals: current budget consumption rate, candidate model latency overhead, and variance in candidate outputs. Controller reduces sampling for high-cost or high-variance tenants and raises it cautiously when signals stabilize.
- Isolation and quarantine: if a candidate model or tenant crosses safety thresholds (replica-error-rate, replica-latency spike, or anomalous output rates), automatically quarantine the tenant->candidate mapping and notify SRE/PM. Quarantine is soft (no blocking of production traffic) and maintains an audit trail.
- Observability: emit metrics for replica-requests, replica-cost-accumulated, replica-errors, replica-latency, and per-tenant sampling fraction. Surface these in Console with per-route and per-tenant graphs and alerts.
- Auto-rollback triggers: define deterministic triggers based on replica-error-rate, downstream SLA violations, and cost burn velocity. If triggers fire for a model rollout, initiate an automatic rollback of the rollout (canary -> baseline) and mark the rollout as failed in the rollout store.

Implementation notes: implement routing logic as a sidecar/routing service to minimize changes to gateway. Use Redis for soft budget counters with periodic reconciliation to long-term ledger. Provide a feature flag and tenant allowlist for the initial rollout. Integrate with existing rollout service so that canary policies can request replica-routing for controlled tenants.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Using soft counters (Redis) yields lower write cost but weaker absolute accounting — acceptable because budget enforcement is intended to be conservative and complemented by billing reconciliation.
- Placing logic in a routing service centralizes policy but adds a single point to scale; we'll horizontally scale the router and make it stateless where possible.
- Adaptive sampling reduces cost but can bias evaluation if not tuned; acceptance tests include synthetic replay to ensure representativeness.

Testing and rollout plan:
1) Unit tests + load tests for router at 10k rps with mixed tenant distribution.
2) Synthetic replay against candidate models to verify signal quality under KV-cache effects.
3) Canary rollout on non-critical tenants (1% of tenants) with strict budgets and human-in-the-loop for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual expansion to 10% then 25% with automated budget adjustments.

Expected metrics of success: lower replication cost volatility (95th percentile daily cost delta reduced by 60%), actionable canary signals (alert precision > 85%), no customer-facing regressions during canary.

Open questions: how to best estimate downstream token cost for multimodal requests; whether budget delta should count only successful replica responses; consistency model for budget reconciliation during outages.
acceptance_criteria: Router accepts tenant-scoped replication policy and enforces sampling fractions per-tenant
Per-tenant budget counters decrease as replicas are issued and prevent further replication when exhausted
Adaptive sampling controller reduces sampling for high-cost tenants and increases safely when stable
Quarantine rule triggers when replica-error-rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes and reported to SRE/PM
Automated rollback integrates with rollout store and can revert canary within configured SLAs
Metrics and dashboards present per-tenant replica cost and sampling fraction in Console
Load test demonstrates router can sustain target throughput with <5ms median added latency
comments: 2025-02-15: Spike complete — measured naive sampling on 10 tenants and observed cost concentration in top-3 tenants. Prototype router implemented as Go service (stateless) and passed functional tests.
2025-02-18: Design review with PM (Lina Ortiz) and SRE (Marcus Liu). Agreed on Redis soft counters and reconciliation job; SRE requested rate-limiting on router write paths to protect Redis.
2025-02-22: Implemented tenant budget model and initial admin UI for top-ups. Draft PR opened (see artifact link). Looking for UX review from Console team before canary.
2025-02-26: Performance run: router adds median 3.8ms latency at 5k rps and scales horizontally. Noted increased variance for requests with long sequences; flagged as follow-up (ENG-33376).
2025-03-01: PM requested a conservative default sampling policy: 0.5% global with tenant caps. We added per-tenant cap enforcement to avoid accidental large-scale replication.
2025-03-02: Preparing canary on 1% of tenants next week; SRE to enable alerting for replica-cost-accumulated and auto-quarantine thresholds.
